name: CertChain
tagline: Decentralized certificate verification on Ethereum + IPFS
about: CertChain is a hybrid on-chain/off-chain decentralized application for issuing and verifying academic certificates. It combines Ethereum smart contracts with IPFS-backed decentralized storage through Pinata.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: CertChain is a decentralized application (DApp) for issuing and verifying academic certificates. It uses a hybrid on-chain/off-chain architecture: certificate files are stored on IPFS via Pinata, while their metadata hashes are permanently recorded on the Ethereum blockchain.

sections.heading: The Problem
sections.body: Traditional academic certificates are difficult to verify at scale. Paper certificates can be forged, digital copies can be altered, and the verification process typically requires contacting the issuing institution directly — a slow, manual, and unreliable workflow.

sections.heading: Why Blockchain?
sections.body: Blockchain provides an immutable, publicly verifiable ledger. Once a certificate hash is written to Ethereum, it cannot be altered without changing the hash — making forgery detectable. The decentralized nature means verification does not depend on any single institution's system being online.

sections.heading: System Architecture
sections.body: The system has two main data paths. The file path: React Frontend → Express Backend → IPFS/Pinata (file storage). The blockchain path: React Frontend → Ethers.js → Ethereum Smart Contract (hash storage). MetaMask handles wallet connection and transaction signing in the browser.

sections.heading: Certificate Issuance
sections.body: An administrator enters certificate information and uploads the certificate PDF or image. The backend streams the file to IPFS through Pinata, which returns an immutable CID. Metadata is generated, a SHA-256 hash is calculated, and the Certificate ID plus hash are written to the Ethereum smart contract via a MetaMask-signed transaction.

sections.heading: Verification
sections.body: A user enters a Certificate ID or hash. The system performs a blockchain lookup to retrieve the stored hash, fetches metadata from the backend, validates the SHA-256 hash, and retrieves the original file from IPFS. Three verification layers provide confidence: blockchain reference, SHA-256 metadata hash, and IPFS CID integrity.

sections.heading: Batch Issuance
sections.body: The system supports batch certificate issuance by parsing CSV data with PapaParse. Multiple certificates can be submitted in a single blockchain transaction, reducing gas costs and administrative overhead.

sections.heading: Security & Integrity
sections.body: Certificate integrity relies on three independent layers: the Ethereum blockchain reference (immutable hash record), SHA-256 metadata hashing (detects tampering), and IPFS CID integrity (content-addressed storage ensures the retrieved file matches exactly what was stored). A QR code encodes the verification URL for easy physical-to-digital bridging.

sections.heading: Technical Challenges
sections.body: Coordinating asynchronous operations across three systems — the React frontend, Express backend, and Ethereum node via MetaMask — required careful state management to handle transaction confirmations, IPFS upload progress, and error states gracefully.
